activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use the present simple correctly?

options.text: She works in a café.
They lives near here.
I walk to school.
He go by train.

activities.explanation: «She works» and «I walk» agree with their subjects; the other two need «live» and «go».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: I saw a dog in the park.
She bought an useful guide.
We visited the museum yesterday.
He needs a information.

activities.explanation: «A dog» and «the museum» are correct; use «a useful guide» and «some information» for the other sentences.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use past simple correctly?

options.text: We visited York last summer.
She buyed a ticket.
They saw the exhibition.
He goed home early.

activities.explanation: «Visited» and irregular «saw» are correct past forms; the others need «bought» and «went».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: I do not understand the map.
He don't like coffee.
They do not need help.
She not works here.

activities.explanation: «Do not» agrees with «I» and «they»; «he doesn't» and «she doesn't work» are needed in the others.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use basic prepositions correctly?

options.text: The keys are on the table.
We arrived in the station.
She is at home.
He waited at the bus.

activities.explanation: Use «on the table» and «at home»; the other phrases need «at the station» and «for the bus».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use present perfect with a duration or starting point correctly?

options.text: I have lived here for two years.
She has worked here since March.
He has seen her yesterday.
They have arrived last night.

activities.explanation: «For two years» and «since March» connect past situations to the present; finished times need past simple.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which questions are formed correctly with «did»?

options.text: Did you see the notice?
Did she went home?
Did they call the office?
Did he bought a pass?

activities.explanation: After «did», use the base forms «see» and «call», not «went» or «bought».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which indirect questions have the correct word order?

options.text: Do you know where the bank is?
Can you tell me where is the bank?
I wonder what time the shop opens.
She asked when does the bus leave.

activities.explanation: Indirect questions use statement order after «where», «what» and «when».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: We have been here since noon.
I have known her for 2019.
He has studied for three months.
They have lived here since five years.

activities.explanation: «Since» takes a starting point and «for» takes a duration.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use countable and uncountable nouns correctly?

options.text: There is some useful information here.
There are many reasons to wait.
I need an advice.
She bought much books.

activities.explanation: «Information» is uncountable and «reasons» is plural countable; use «some advice» and «many books» in the others.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: Although it was late, we continued.
Despite it was late, we continued.
We left because the shop was closing.
We left because of the shop was closing.

activities.explanation: «Although» takes a clause and «because» introduces a clause; «despite» takes a noun or gerund, while «because of» takes a noun phrase.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: The room was cleaned yesterday.
The forms have been signed.
The bridge was build in 1900.
The letters are send every Friday.

activities.explanation: The correct participles are «cleaned» and «signed»; the others need «built» and «sent».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use the verb patterns correctly?

options.text: She explained the rule to me.
He suggested going by train.
She explained me the rule.
He suggested to go by train.

activities.explanation: «Explain» takes «to me» and «suggest» is followed by a gerund in this pattern.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: Mia said that she was tired.
Mia told that she was tired.
Mia told us that she was tired.
Mia said us that she was tired.

activities.explanation: Use «said that» without a person object or «told us that» with one.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use verb + gerund patterns correctly?

options.text: I enjoy reading on the train.
She avoids eating late.
They enjoy to read together.
He avoids to answer the question.

activities.explanation: «Enjoy» and «avoid» are followed by gerunds in these examples.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: If I were you, I would wait.
If she had time, she would join us.
If I would be you, I waited.
If he has time, he would joined us.

activities.explanation: The second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause and «would + base verb» in the result.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: It was so cold that we stayed inside.
It was such a cold day that we stayed inside.
It was so a cold day that we stayed inside.
It was such cold that we stayed inside.

activities.explanation: Use «so + adjective» and «such + a/an + adjective + noun».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: Nora said that she was busy.
Nora told me that she was busy.
Nora said me that she was busy.
Nora told that she was busy.

activities.explanation: «Said that» has no direct person object; «told me that» includes one.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use «wish» for past regret correctly?

options.text: I wish I had checked the time.
She wishes she had brought a coat.
I wish I would checked the time.
She wishes she has brought a coat.

activities.explanation: Past regret uses «wish + past perfect»: «had checked» and «had brought».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: The form must be signed today.
The figures should be checked.
The form must signed today.
The figures should be check.

activities.explanation: A modal passive needs «modal + be + past participle».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: The bridge is believed to be safe.
The castle is thought to have been built in 1800.
The bridge is believed be safe.
The castle is thought to have build in 1800.

activities.explanation: The reporting passive uses «to be» for a current state and «to have been built» for a completed past action.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: No sooner had we arrived than it started raining.
The evidence is consistent with the report.
No sooner had we arrived when it started raining.
The evidence is consistent to the report.

activities.explanation: The fixed patterns are «no sooner ... than» and «consistent with».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use articles with general and specific reference correctly?

options.text: Water is essential for life.
The water in this bottle is cold.
The water is essential for life.
A water in this bottle is cold.

activities.explanation: No article is used for water in general; «the water» refers to a specific amount.

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.
activities.prompt: Which sentences use prepositions in fixed patterns correctly?

options.text: She apologised for being late.
They are responsible for the keys.
She apologised about being late.
They are responsible of the keys.

activities.explanation: The standard patterns are «apologise for» and «responsible for».

activities.instructions: Select all the grammatically correct sentences.

options.text: Despite the rain, we walked home.
Despite being tired, she finished the form.
Despite it was raining, we walked home.
Despite of the delay, we waited.

activities.explanation: «Despite» takes a noun phrase or gerund, without «of» or a full clause directly after it.
